acip: GNYIS PA 'KHOR BSKYED TSUL NI, MTHA' SKOR RIM BZHIN, ZHES PA NAS, RDO RJE GSUM MTSAN ZHES PA'I BAR RKANG PA PHYED DANG GSUM STE, KHROM 'TSOGS MTHO BRTZEGS GNYIS LAS 'DIR KHROM 'TSOGS YIN PAS,
wylie: gnyis pa 'khor bskyed tshul ni, mtha' skor rim bzhin, zhes pa nas, rdo rje gsum mtshan zhes pa'i bar rkang pa phyed dang gsum ste, khrom 'tshogs mtho brtsegs gnyis las 'dir khrom 'tshogs yin pas
english: [27 continued...] This brings us to our second point from above, on how we bring forth our Lama's retinue.  This is presented in the four and a half lines of the translation which begin with "Surrounding Him are rows..." and continue up to "...the three doors of expression."  There are two traditional ways of visualizing this retinue--in a crowd as you might see in an open market; and in groups like terraces.  What we use here is the former.
